records.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR Viper GTS-R maps to the final ORECA-supported Chrysler Viper GTS-R specification represented in PMR's 2004-era GT content. PMR describes this car as a Chrysler Viper GTS-R developed with ORECA and lists a six-speed sequential transmission. Period ORECA technical commentary confirms that GTS-R customer cars existed with both the classic six-speed Tremec and later sequential dog-type options, so the exact chassis and gearbox installation matter. The PMR staged H-pattern is therefore retained as simulator evidence and is not promoted as the authentic baseline without an exact-chassis match. Keep the road-going Dodge Viper GTS-R/GT2 Championship Edition, earlier H-pattern race configurations, and the later 2012 SRT Viper GTS-R distinct.
records.confidence_basis: The official PMR car page names Chrysler Viper GTS-R, says it was developed with ORECA, places it in the 2004-era GT content, and lists six-speed sequential transmission. A period interview with ORECA's technical representative independently confirms the Viper GTS-R family and documents the coexistence of classic and sequential racing gearbox options. No matching curated record exists in data/v1, so this case proposes a new canonical identity while preserving the configuration uncertainty.

PMR's target page explicitly lists six-speed sequential transmission, and the ORECA interview confirms sequential gearbox options as the common later customer installation. The generic family T56 entry is retained as a configuration warning rather than applied to the PMR target. The observed PMR standard-H gate is kept as implementation evidence only.
